name: CA-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting D+7 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at 97%
McGuire has outraised Gallagher with outside support
Gallagher's incumbency provides only a modest offset
model.rationale: The redrawn district leans Democratic by seven points, and prediction markets price a Democratic win near certainty. McGuire's fundraising edge and outside support outweigh Gallagher's incumbency, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-implied double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Gallagher running competitively ahead of the incumbent advantage, or a major shift in the national environment, could move this toward Lean D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 1st District was redrawn to lean Democratic by about seven points, putting incumbent Republican James Gallagher on difficult new terrain. Gallagher, a state legislator before winning this seat, has raised about $1.5 million, but Democratic state senator Mike McGuire has raised more, roughly $1.8 million, and benefits from about $600,000 in outside support with no outside opposition spending against him.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on the district's fundamentals and market pricing. Polymarket gives McGuire roughly a 97% chance, consistent with a double-digit Democratic margin. Incumbency gives Gallagher a small cushion, but the redrawn electorate points clearly toward McGuire, making this a Safe Democratic race with modest residual uncertainty from the lack of polling.
